headline: Fields Medal-winning mathematician Terence Tao is at the centre of the argument over what AI will mean for the future of mathematics.
score_reason: Prominent mathematician in a live debate over AI-made proofs; no new result; topic confirmed by The Indian Express, the Times article itself not seen.
importance_line: What counts as progress in mathematics is being rethought as AI produces proofs at scale, which affects researchers, journals and students, and Tao's warning is one prominent view in a field where others doubt that AI-made proofs are valuable or even correct.
summary: The New York Times describes Terence Tao, a Fields Medal-winning mathematician, as being on the front lines of the debate over AI and the future of math, and The Indian Express reports that in a 9 Oct 2026 lecture at Caltech he said that “further blind optimization of problem-solving alone is now actively harmful to the long-term health of mathematics.” He sees open problems as guides to explore rather than destinations, and warns that reaching them too fast with automated tools could crowd out the ideas that appear along the way.
notes: Headline only for the NYT piece; context from The Indian Express (https://indianexpress.com/article/explained/explained-ai/ai-in-mathematics-terence-tao-proof-verification-10920833/).
